scenario.description: A securities finance committee chair must decide whether to authorize a proposed securities loan and finalize the loan size, collateral structure, settlement timing, margin process, term, and collateral-use rights, with input from risk, compliance, operations, and client coverage.

shared_context.S1: A hedge fund has requested to borrow $8,000,000 of the bank's investment-grade corporate bonds for a proposed 30-day term.
shared_context.S2: The draft transaction would take $9,000,000 of mixed cash and government-bond collateral, permit collateral reuse, and use the desk's standard settlement and margin process.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding authorization decision for the securities loan.
shared_context.S4: Under the committee's normal pre-trade routine, Elena asks risk, compliance, collateral operations, and client coverage to report any relevant conditions before authorizing the transaction.
shared_context.S5: When a revised numeric or categorical transaction parameter is required, the revised value must be reflected in the settlement decisions themselves, not merely noted as a follow-up condition for a future proposal.
shared_context.S6: When all required revised parameters can be reflected directly in the settlement decisions, committee practice is to authorize the transaction with those revised parameters rather than require a resubmission.

PF1.text: Marcus confirmed in a counterparty review completed this morning that the hedge fund already has $3,000,000 of exposure across other securities-finance trades; the applicable aggregate limit is $10,000,000, so this trade can add no more than $7,000,000. The exposure total has not yet been updated in the committee worksheet.

PF2.text: Nadia received a compliance memo this morning stating that this fund's collateral for corporate-bond borrowing must be cash only and must equal at least 105% of the loaned securities' value; the rule has not yet been added to the desk checklist.

PF3.text: Jonah's settlement-system test completed this week shows that this counterparty can settle collateral only on T+1 and requires a daily margin call; the test result is still in his operations folder rather than the trade ticket.

PF4.text: Leila found in the client's lending mandate while reviewing the account this week that any loan of these bonds may run for no more than 14 days and that the borrower may not reuse the collateral; she has not yet attached the mandate extract to the transaction file.

acceptance_conditions: The securities loan must be authorized for exactly $7,000,000 of bonds.
The collateral must be cash only and equal exactly $7,350,000.
The transaction must settle on T+1 and require daily margining.
The loan term must be exactly 14 days.
The settlement must include commitments documenting daily margining and the collateral-use restriction.
The counterparty exposure limit must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C9: any('daily margin' in c['detail'] or 'Daily margin' in c['detail'] or 'DAILY MARGIN' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any('reuse' in c['detail'] or 'Reuse' in c['detail'] or 'REUSE' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public request is for $8,000,000, but PF1 changes the permitted incremental loan amount to exactly $7,000,000 because $3,000,000 of existing exposure consumes part of the $10,000,000 aggregate limit.
The draft permits mixed collateral of $9,000,000, while PF2 changes the required form to cash only and the required amount to exactly 105% of $7,000,000, or $7,350,000.

The standard process does not specify this counterparty's mechanics, while PF3 changes settlement to exactly T+1, requires daily margining, and requires a settlement commitment documenting daily margining.

The draft uses a 30-day term and permits reuse, while PF4 changes the permitted term to exactly 14 days, requires collateral_reuse_allowed to be false, and requires a commitment documenting the collateral-use restriction.
